chapter: Louis Armstrong picture, Kid Rena record and Bunk
title: Louis Armstrong as a boy: bugle, slide whistle, natural humor
summary: Rene recalls knowing Louis as a boy playing bugle and slide whistle, always joking and natural.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When you knew Louie as a boy, what instruments did he play? You say he played bugle and cornet?
Bugle. You know when the slide whistle? Mm-hmm. Boy, he was ace on there. Boy, he could play that slide whistle.
Boy, he was a kid. And what about, uh, could he, you ever hear him play piano?

No, I never heard him play piano. He might have picked it up maybe when he got married, eh? I tell you one thing, though, that fellow, you see him? All the way he came on, that's just natural. They know put no, they know nothing to add on to his life. That's just natural. And that's the way he always was, from a kid. I know him from a kid. Always joking, killing, and laughing, make all kinds of spaces and everything. That's natural. That ain't nothing, no, no put on, no special gestures. Nothing, that's just natural. Natural with him.
